svg.desc: Banner for linear coordinate presentations of Lotka–Volterra tree systems. Left: the tree system on the path 1–2–3 from Example 1.1 of the paper, x1′ = x1(2x2 + 4x3), x2′ = x2(x1 + 4x3), x3′ = x3(x1 + 3x2). Besides the three coordinate planes it has exactly two further invariant planes, one per edge of the tree: Q12 = x1 − 2x2 for edge 1–2 and Q23 = 3x2 − 4x3 for edge 2–3, giving 2n − 1 = 5 in all. Centre: the positive orthant seen projectively as a triangle (the chart x1 + x2 + x3 = 1). The three coordinate planes are its sides, and the two edge planes are the exact lines x1 = 2x2 and 3x2 = 4x3, which meet inside the triangle. Grey curves are orbits of the equation computed numerically for illustration; none crosses any of the five lines. Right: the cone over the tree, a vertex 0 joined to vertices 1, 2 and 3; its three spokes correspond to the coordinate planes and its two tree edges to Q12 and Q23. Any three planes forming a spanning tree of the cone can serve as new coordinates, and there are 8 such choices. Choosing x1, x2, x3 gives extra supports {1,2} and {2,3}, a tree. Choosing x1, Q12, Q23, as in the paper’s example, gives supports {1,2} and {1,2,3}, a hypergraph. It is the same equation in two presentations. For generic parameters the five planes determine the tree, which is why two different trees never give the same generic equation; an extension to special parameter values fails.
svg.text: grey: computed orbits; none crosses a line
8 choices = spanning trees of the cone over the tree
for generic parameters the five planes determine the tree
